title: Microsoft Teams: redesigned header and dashboard for chats and channels on mobile
summary: The briefing matches the roadmap and Microsoft's updated tenant notice, including the automatic rollout and expected completion window. The product licensing statement is supported, and independent searches found no documented switch for this mobile redesign.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model; licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence
claims.claim: The licensing model is included as a new screen inside the already licensed Teams mobile app.
claims.quote: All supported subscription plans are eligible for access to the Teams web client, desktop clients, and mobile apps. Teams is available as part of qualifying Microsoft 365 offerings and as a standalone SKU.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing: Licence; rationale: cost
claims.claim: No separate licence or charge specific to this redesign is published in the sources checked.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile updated header dashboard chats channels licensing additional license charge pricing meter. Opened Teams service description; read roadmap and MC1467357; reviewed Learn search results. No redesign-specific licence or charge found.

claims.where: Cost and licensing: Meter
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap item nor MC1467357 describes a meter for this change.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile updated header dashboard chats channels licensing additional license charge pricing meter. Read the entire roadmap record and MC1467357; opened Teams service description. Neither record describes a meter for this redesign.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and .api; controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: No admin UI setting or PowerShell parameter is documented to govern the redesigned mobile header and dashboard or retain the previous layout.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "mobile" "header" disable dashboard admin. Opened Manage messaging policies in Teams, Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy, Set-CsTeamsMobilityPolicy and Intune configure-teams-mobile; none documents a header/dashboard rollout or old-layout switch.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific redesigned mobile header and dashboard feature.
claims.quote: Searched: "Teams" "mobile" "header" "dashboard"; Teams mobile redesigned header dashboard channel details people pinned content iOS Android. Read results and opened messaging policies and mobile app configuration; no feature-specific Learn page found.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The messaging policy setting On mobile devices, display favorite channels above recent chats moves favourite channels to the top of the mobile screen.
claims.quote: On mobile devices, display favorite channels above recent chats - Enable this setting to move favorite channels to the top of the mobile device screen so that a user doesn't need to scroll to find them.

claims.where: Governance controls
claims.claim: The favourite-channel ordering setting is not documented as governing the redesigned chat and channel header or dashboard.
claims.quote: Searched: Teams mobile redesigned header lightweight dashboard chats channels admin disable opt out previous layout policy PowerShell. Opened messaging policies and Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy; ChannelsInChatListEnabledType controls favourite-channel ordering, not this redesign.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: MC1467357 identifies no compliance considerations.
claims.quote: No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: MC1467357 describes easier access to content rather than describing new data access.
claims.quote: Searched: new data access in the supplied MC1467357 text. Read the complete notice: it describes easier access to channel details, people and pinned content and identifies no compliance considerations; it states no new data access.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity
claims.claim: Neither the roadmap item nor MC1467357 mentions changes to sign-in, permissions or identity.
claims.quote: Searched: sign-in, permissions and identity in the supplied roadmap record and MC1467357. Read both in full; neither describes changes to these subjects.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions
claims.claim: The sources describe a navigation surface and do not describe it acting autonomously on a user's behalf.
claims.quote: Searched: autonomous actions and acting on a user's behalf in the roadmap, MC1467357 and fetched Learn pages. The records describe users finding information and taking action; no autonomous dashboard actions are described.

claims.where: Scope: Prerequisites
claims.claim: The roadmap item and MC1467357 name no additional prerequisites beyond using Teams on mobile.
claims.quote: Searched: prerequisites in the supplied roadmap record and MC1467357. Read both in full: they identify Teams mobile users and say no action is required, with no additional prerequisite named.
